hook.text: Some of the richest fishing grounds sit where cold, deep water rises to the surface.

buildup.text: When wind pushes surface water away from shore, deep water rises to replace it—this is upwelling.

discovery.text: Upwelled water is cold and loaded with nutrients that fuel explosive plankton growth.

twist.text: During El Niño, upwelling off Peru weakens—fish populations crash and economies suffer.

climax.text: Upwelling zones cover less than 1% of the ocean but support about 50% of global fish catches.

punchline.text: The ocean's richest waters come from its deepest layers.

quiz.question: What does upwelling bring to the surface?
